notes: Confluence tables and headings imported whole

entries.title: Confluence tables and headings imported whole
entries.detail: A table whose row headers hold paragraphs no longer breaks apart into text with "|" signs, and a heading that starts with a line break or holds a table of contents stays one heading. Import the space again to get the fixed pages.

entries.title: Columns in a page: one, two or three
entries.detail: The toolbar has One column, Two columns and Three columns. Two or three put empty columns below the line you are on; in columns they change how many there are, and One column puts everything back on the page, nothing lost. On a narrow page the columns stand one below the other. A Confluence import now keeps the columns of a page, as on the space's home page. New tools: if you set up your toolbar yourself, add them in Settings › Toolbar.

entries.title: Document pictures in a Confluence import, with no extra step
entries.detail: In the Mac app, Import Confluence export… now draws the picture of each Word, PowerPoint or PDF page that Confluence shows, by itself, and puts it above the file, also in a table cell. No script to run first.

entries.title: A new page opens at once, also after an import
entries.detail: A page that folia opened while it was still saving it could say "No access to this page" until a reload, for example the home page right after a Confluence import. folia now asks again a second later and opens it.

entries.title: A Confluence import that looks like Confluence
entries.detail: Import Confluence export… now keeps what Confluence draws in the browser: the page trees and child page lists, tables of contents, recent updates, version history and file lists. Coloured text keeps its colour, a row's own header is bold, and a price like $5 / $30 stays text.

entries.title: Calmer marks for commented words
entries.detail: Words with a comment now sit on a soft grey pill instead of an amber line. The words of the comment you have open get a slightly stronger grey.

entries.title: Comments: jump to the words, and @ to mention
entries.detail: Click a comment in the Comments window, and the page goes to the words it is about, with them selected. Typing @ in a comment or a reply opens the same list of people as in the page; pick one with the mouse or Enter.

entries.title: All side windows the same width
entries.detail: Comments on the right is now as wide as Meetings, Outline and History, so the page keeps the same room whichever side window is open.

entries.title: Picking a tabula task works every time
entries.detail: In the Link tabula task box, a task is picked as soon as you press it, and a press anywhere in the box keeps it open. A long list moves above the cursor when there is no room below, so it stays in the window.

entries.title: Many new pages at once all show
entries.detail: When many pages arrive at once, from an import or from someone else's work, folia now shows them all together. Before, from about 50 at once, a few could be missing from the list until folia was opened again.

entries.title: Find a tabula task from the page
entries.detail: Type /task in a page, or use the tool Link tabula task: a field searches your tabula tasks by name or number, and a pick puts the task's link in the page with its state beside it. With words selected, the words become the link. The pill beside a task link now opens the task too, and in the Mac app a task link opens the tabula app instead of the website.

entries.title: Import a Confluence space
entries.detail: A notebook's … menu › Import Confluence export… (also in ⌘K) takes the zip of a Confluence space's HTML export. The space's home page becomes the wiki's home page, each page under it a section, and a page with pages under it a page group. Text, tables, code, info boxes, pictures and attached files come along; links between the pages become folia links. Files a page has attached but does not show are listed under Attachments at its end.

entries.title: Greyed-out tools say why
entries.detail: Point at a tool that is greyed out, and it says what to do: Create tabula task asks you to select some words first, Fold-out heading to put the cursor in a heading, and the alignment tools say they do not work in a list, a quote or a table.

entries.title: No more amber @mentions, and a list that fits
entries.detail: A mention of you is now the same quiet grey pill as every other @mention. The list that opens when you type @ is as wide as its names, so a name stays on one line, and an address shows in the normal font.

entries.title: Calmer @mentions, and the right colour for who is here
entries.detail: An @mention in a page or a comment is now a quiet grey pill with no line under it, as folia's style guide draws a pill. A mention of you has an amber edge, so you see it at once. The name beside a page's dates that shows who else is on the page now has the same colour as that person's face in Settings › Users.

entries.title: Pick people when you share
entries.detail: The Share window of a notebook or wiki space lists the people you can add, with their face, name and address, as tabula does. Type a few letters of a name or an address to find someone, choose Can edit or Can read, and press Add. A new e-mail address still works with Share.

entries.title: Choose the top bar's buttons
entries.detail: Settings › Top bar shows the buttons at the top right as the top bar draws them. Click a button to take it out or put it back, drag it to a new place, or press ← → on it. Settings always stays at the right end, and the keys and ⌘K still work for a button you took out. Back to the start brings all of them back.

entries.title: tabula tasks in a page
entries.detail: Paste a link to a tabula task into a page: beside it, folia shows the task's number, its state, the date it is due and who owns it, as tabula has it now. Select words and use Create tabula task (add it in Settings › Toolbar, or above a selection): the words become a new task in your tabula Review, and a link to it.

entries.title: Fold-out headings
entries.detail: A heading can fold the text under it, up to the next heading of its level, for an FAQ or long details. Add the tool Fold-out heading in Settings › Toolbar, put the cursor in a heading and press it. An arrow before the heading opens and closes it. People who can only read see it folded at first; folia remembers what you opened. In the Markdown file it is a small hidden note on the heading's line, so other apps show everything.

entries.title: Links to this page, in wiki spaces
entries.detail: At the foot of a page in a wiki space, folia lists the pages that link to it with [[ ]], each with its notebook and section. A click opens one. Plain notebooks stay without the list.

entries.title: Page owners and review dates
entries.detail: In a wiki space, a page's … menu has Owner and review…: who keeps the page up to date, and how often to look at it. When that time has come, the page says it may be out of date, its owner is told in the bell, and Mark as reviewed starts the time again. Search › In › Need review lists such pages.

entries.title: @mentions and notifications
entries.detail: Type @ in a page and pick a person: their name shows as a coloured pill. In a comment, write @ and their name. The person is told in the new bell at the top, also of replies in their threads and new comments on pages they made. A click opens the page, and the thread when there is one.

entries.title: Comments
entries.detail: The new Comments button in the top bar opens the comments of the page. Select words and write a comment on them, or comment on the whole page. The words get a soft mark; a click on them opens their thread. Everyone in the notebook can reply and mark a thread as resolved, also people who can only read; you can change and delete your own comments. The button shows how many threads are open.

entries.title: Wiki spaces
entries.detail: The owner of a notebook can make it a wiki space in its … menu. It gets a book in place of its letter, its sections and pages stay where you put them, and it opens on its home page, which any page's … menu can set. Above each page's title a line shows where it is; each part takes you there.

entries.title: Share a notebook to read only
entries.detail: In Share, each person can edit the notebook or only read it. A reader sees every page and can search it, but cannot type, rename, move or delete anything, and the status bar says "Read only". The owner can change it at any time, and an open page follows at once.

entries.title: A bigger leaf in the Dock and the menu bar
entries.detail: folia's leaf is a little bigger in its app icon, and fills the menu bar's height. So it now has the same size as the marks of your other apps.

entries.title: Only new briefs are made
entries.detail: folia makes a brief only for a meeting or page that has none. A brief it made once stays as it is, also after a day; press Read again in its card for a new one.

entries.title: folia stays quick with a brief on every page and 2 more
entries.detail: folia stays quick with a brief on every page: With briefs on all your knowledge bases, folia could slow down and stop with "Something went wrong". It worked out the list of briefed pages again at each change of any page, which took almost a second; now it takes a hundredth of that. At each start it also read every kept brief again; now it only asks which pages have none. Meetings finds pages the calendar renamed: When your calendar gives a meeting series a new id, Meetings still shows Open for the page you prepared, and does not offer Prepare again. folia finds it by the meeting's time and the title it had at Prepare, also when you changed the page's title. A link from scripta finds it the same way. No Brief button in Meetings: folia reads the briefs by itself, so Meetings shows only Prepare or Open. A meeting's brief is in its page, once you have prepared it.

entries.title: Calendar integration can be switched off
entries.detail: Settings › Mac app has a new switch, Calendar integration, as in tabula. On, Meetings shows the meetings of your Mac's Calendar app, with Prepare and Brief beside each. Off, folia reads no calendar, and Meetings says so. The briefs of your pages are read either way.

entries.title: All briefs are read without a long pause
entries.detail: When folia stops reading the missing briefs because Cerebrum could not answer for a moment, it now tries again after a minute instead of half an hour. So all your pages get their brief soon after the start, without a press on the card.

entries.title: Briefs for all your knowledge bases
entries.detail: With Brief from Cerebrum on, the pages of every notebook whose Markdown copy is in a knowledge base of your vault now get the brief card too, such as your NZZ and SRG SSR notebooks, not only the ETH ones. folia reads the missing briefs one page at a time, the newest first; Settings › Armarium shows how far it is.

entries.title: Choose where your Cerebrum vault is
entries.detail: Settings › Armarium › Cerebrum has a new row, Vault folder. Brief from Cerebrum reads your vault from the standard place in iCloud Drive, or from any folder you choose on this Mac, so a vault anywhere works, also another person's. The briefs are kept in the briefs folder of that vault. The row also says when a folder has no Cerebrum vault, or when the vault does not let folia keep briefs yet.

entries.title: Safer files, and a quicker page list
entries.detail: A stored file that could run code, such as an HTML or SVG file, now downloads instead of opening in a browser tab. In the Mac app, a program, script or installer shows in the Finder instead of opening. A picture added to a Markdown file whose _assets folder is not there yet now goes into that folder. folia reads your page list in fewer, quicker steps.

entries.title: scripta writes into the page you prepared
entries.detail: scripta's minutes, Prepare and the meetings panel find a meeting's page also when the calendar changed the meeting's id, had the meeting twice, or the page was made by hand for that day. A new page for the meeting goes to the section of its series.

entries.title: Changes by others are marked row by row in tables
entries.detail: When someone changes a cell, the bar beside the page now marks only that row, not the whole table. Rows in a row changed by one person share one bar, and ⌘G and the arrows go from row to row.

entries.title: Briefs are read in a moment
entries.detail: folia now keeps one Cerebrum reader open instead of starting it for every question. A page that has no brief yet gets one in about a second, and the pass over your ETH pages takes minutes instead of hours.

entries.title: A brief on every page of your ETH notebooks, on both Macs
entries.detail: With Brief from Cerebrum on, every page of your ETH notebooks gets the folded brief card: what Cerebrum knows about its topic, the open items, and what was still open on the page before it in the section. folia reads the missing briefs one page at a time, the newest first; Settings › Armarium shows how far it is. The briefs are kept in your Cerebrum vault, in its own folder briefs, so your other Mac shows them too without reading them again.

entries.title: Align text left, centre, right or justified and 2 more
entries.detail: Align text left, centre, right or justified: As in Word, for text and headings: add the four tools to the toolbar in Settings › Toolbar, or give them keys in Settings › Keys. A second press of Centre, Right or Justify goes back to left. The alignment stays in History, copies and templates, and the Markdown copy writes it as GitHub does. Lists, quotes and tables keep their own alignment. Choose the tools above a selection: Settings › Toolbar now also sets what shows above selected words: the font colours as before, and any of Bold, Italic, Link, the alignments, headings, lists and more, in your order. Its switch moved there from Settings › General. ⌘G goes through the changes by others: With nothing in the search field, ⌘G goes to the next place someone else changed on the open page, and ⇧⌘G to the one before. With words in the search field, ⌘G still goes through the hits.

entries.title: A person's face beside their changes
entries.detail: The bars beside what others wrote now carry the person's face from Settings › Users: the first letter of their address, in their colour. The line under the title and Share use the same face. A colour chosen in Settings › Users shows on the page at once. Beside older text the bar is lighter, the face stays in full colour.

entries.title: Who wrote what, whenever you want
entries.detail: Switch on Who wrote what in Settings › General, or in ⌘K: every page then shows a bar beside everything others wrote, in their colour, not only what is new. What is new since you last read the page stays bright, the rest is lighter.
